title.narrative: Response to the Forcibly Displaced Myanmar Nationals and Host Community

description.narrative:
After four years following the the exodus of Rohingyas from Myanmar, more than 900,000 are still living in temporary settlements spread across 34 congested camps in Cox’s Bazar District, Bangladesh. In their current circumstances, they lack formal legal status, face extreme restrictions on movement and are not permitted to legally work. The refugee influx overwhelmed the existing response capacity and put immense strain on infrastructure, services, resources and the local environment, and the extreme level of humanitarian needs has not decreased. The Government of Bangladesh and local communities have supported the refugees to the best of their ability, but solidarity has been strained, especially in the last two years.
Caritas Bangladesh (CB) was one of the first humanitarian actors to respond in 2017, and has been continuously responding to the emergency needs of Rohingya refugees since then through food and NFI distributions, shelter construction, settlement planning and upgrading, provision of WASH facilities, and community-based protection for families and children. During the last 4 years (September 2017 – December 2021), Caritas Bangladesh has reached more than 1.2 million individuals.
In 2022, Caritas Bangladesh plans to assist more than 230,000 Rohingya refugees and people from host communities in Cox’s Bazaar district through integrated Shelter/Site development, WASH, DRR, Livelihoods, Protection, and education services. The activities proposed in this appeal respond to assessed gaps and needs identified by the humanitarian community under the coordination of the ISCG in the 2022 Joint Response Plan. Caritas Bangladesh, with the assistance of its numerous partners, especially Caritas Internationalis Member Organizations, is positioned to effectively and efficiently implement this project with high quality and accountability. Along with other Caritas agencies, CAFOD is providing funding to Caritas Bangladesh to enable this important work.
